name: Cellini
lede: Cellini is a deep red-violet in an old color chart, and our books do not explain the name.

sections.title: A name without a story
sections.body:
The color Cellini appears in the Maerz & Paul dictionary of 1930 [2]. Our books do not say who it was named for, and a link to any particular person is undocumented. The only Cellini that Birren mentions is Benvenuto Cellini, a sixteenth-century artist whom he cites on the subject of auras, not paint [1].

On screen the swatch is a strong magenta-purple, close to the family of [[plum]], [[dark-purple]] and [[mauve]], though much deeper than any of them. Its closest chromatic relatives on our charts are [[corinthian-purple]] and [[carnation]], and the pale [[pink]] end of the same hue range.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least one per cent of its canvas [3]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole, and every number is as photographed.

notes.cite: Birren, Color Psychology and Color Therapy, ch. 4 ("The Aural Healers")
